gp-2024-11-hartland.title: Lights on at Hartland
gp-2024-11-hartland.place: Hartland Caravan and Camping Park, North Devon
gp-2024-11-hartland.caption:
A November weekend away for Ted & Lola at Hartland Caravan and Camping Park. We rolled in on the Friday evening and got the lights and the windbreak up.
On the Saturday we walked about 8 miles there and back to Hartland Quay, with a well-earned beer at the Hartland Quay Hotel at the halfway point. That evening we ate at the Hart Inn, and the food was excellent. We all went for the fillet of beef Wellington off the specials board and got the last of it: huge, and really tasty.
Home on the Sunday over Exmoor, with the dashboard crew keeping watch 🩶🤍

gp-2025-05-croyde.title: Sunshine at Croyde
gp-2025-05-croyde.caption:
Ted & Lola pitched up side by side at Camping@Croydebay for a long weekend, with the chairs out and the sun shining.
Sunny walks on the beach, a trip along the coast to Woolacombe, excellent food at Blue Groove and drinks at The Thatch, finished off with a sunset on Croyde beach. The perfect weekend away 🩶🤍

gp-2026-09-kingfisher.title: Kingfisher spotting on the walk into Kendal
gp-2026-09-kingfisher.caption:
We walked into Kendal from the campsite at Sedgwick, following the river most of the way, with the final stretch along the old disused canal, which is now a footpath.
On the way we spotted a kingfisher, something Annette and Ian had never seen in the wild before. Can you spot it? 🩶🤍

gp-2026-09-kendal.title: Five nights at Kendal
gp-2026-09-kendal.place: Kendal Caravan and Motorhome Club Campsite, Sedgwick
gp-2026-09-kendal.caption:
Our base for the first five nights of the Lake District trip was the Kendal Caravan and Motorhome Club site at Sedgwick, just south of Kendal.
There were plenty of walks straight from the campsite: the River Kent rushing past, a little waterfall tucked away in the woods, and a dunnock who stopped by to say hello. From here we also walked into Kendal along the Lancaster Canal and visited Sizergh 🩶🤍

gps-2025-10-llandygai.title: Flying over Penrhyn Quarry
gps-2025-10-llandygai.caption:
Ted & Lola headed to North Wales for a weekend with one big reason: Zip World Velocity 2 at Penrhyn Quarry, near Bethesda. It's billed as the fastest zip line in the world and the longest in Europe, around 1.5 km long, flying face-first over the old slate quarry and its lake at over 100 mph.
Helmets and goggles on, harness checked, and off we went. On the Sunday we stopped in Porthmadog on the way home, at The Australia, the Purple Moose Brewery's pub 🩶🤍

gps-2026-02-portesham.title: A weekend in Weymouth
gps-2026-02-portesham.place: Portesham Dairy Farm Campsite, near Weymouth
gps-2026-02-portesham.caption:
A February weekend away for Ted & Lola, pitched up at Portesham Dairy Farm Campsite, just inland from Weymouth on the Dorset coast. Friday night was a pint or two of King Cnut at the Kings Arms in the village.
On the Saturday we caught the bus into Weymouth for some food, a few beers and a browse around the town 🩶🤍

gps-2026-03-brixham.title: A weekend in Brixham
gps-2026-03-brixham.caption:
A relaxing weekend in Brixham, and the plan was simple: kebabs, steak, darts, cocktails and beer!
Friday started at the Bullers Arms, then on to Liberty, Brixham's original cocktail bar on the quay, and darts to round off the night. We also ate at The Cow Shed, a quirky family-run steak restaurant whose menu runs from steaks and ribs to ostrich, kangaroo and camel. The stocks by the Golden Hind in the harbour were a hit with the criminals among us 🩶🤍
